feature: Timeline dock: no blue outline, and a top edge you drag
summary: The blue rectangle round the timeline is gone. Its top edge now drags like the right panel's edge: up for more tracks, down for more picture, double-click for the height it opened at, remembered between launches.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the Tutorial Sample recording (or any recording) in Edit.

try.do: Open a recording in Edit and look at the timeline: no blue outline round it.
Click the picture, then click the timeline: the dock looks the same either way, and B, I, O, J, K, L still work on the timeline.
Rest the pointer on the line between the picture and the transport: it turns into the up-down resize arrow.
Drag that line up: the timeline grows under the pointer and the picture refits above it.
Drag it all the way down: it stops at the transport, the bar and one track.
Double-click the line: the timeline springs back to its opening height.
Drag it to a height you like, quit and reopen a recording: it opens at that height.

evaluate: Does the edge feel the same as the right panel's edge when you grab it?
Is about 70% of the window the right limit for how tall the timeline can get?
With the outline gone, can you still tell when the keys are going to the timeline rather than the picture?
When you pull the timeline taller than its tracks, is the empty space under them fine, or should it stop at the last track?
rough: The mock draws no resize edge on the timeline; this follows your ask and copies the right panel's edge (a hairline with a 14 point grab strip), so the line itself is as faint as the panel's.
Nothing shows which of the picture or the timeline has the keyboard now. The mock shows nothing either.
Grabbing the edge on its upper half (the part over the picture) hands the keyboard back to the picture, as any click there does.
The walk proves the drags, the floor and the double-click with real pointer events, but it cannot photograph the pointer, so the resize arrow on hover was not seen in a picture.
Reopening a recording in the same test run crashes the test harness (filed separately), so being remembered after a reopen was not walked; it is stored the same way as the panel's width.
